2.q: what was right in the eyes of Yahweh
2.note: The word “eyes” here represents seeing, and seeing represents judgment. Yahweh saw and approved of Joash’s actions. See how you translated a similar phrase in [2 Chronicles 14:1](ta:14). Alternate translation: [what Yahweh judged to be right] or [what Yahweh considered to be right]

2.q: all the days of Jehoiada, the priest
2.note: This idiom means “as long as Jehoiada, the priest, was alive.”

3.q: Jehoiada took for him two wives
3.note: Alternate translation: [Jehoiada chose two wives for Joash]

4.note: This phrase is used here to mark the beginning of a new part of the story. If your language has a way for doing this, you could consider using it here.

5.q: The Levites did nothing at first
5.note: It may be helpful to add “but” to show that the Levites did not obey. Alternate translation: [But the Levites did not do it immediately]

6.q: Why have you not required the Levites … covenant decrees?
6.note: King Joash asks this rhetorical question to accuse Jehoiada of not doing his duty. If it would be helpful in your language, you could express this question as a statement. Alternate translation: [You have neglected your duty. I told you to require the Levites … covenant decrees, but you have not done it.]

6.q: for the tent of the covenant decrees
6.note: Although it refers to the temple that Solomon built, it is a reminder that this tax has been collected since the time of Moses and the “tent of meeting.”

7.note: This refers to the items used for worship in the temple.
Alternate translation: [to people to use for the worship of idols of Baal]

10.q: All the leaders and all the people
10.note: This is a generalization. Some people probably did not respond this way.

11.note: This phrase introduces a new, recurring action. If your language has a way to note this, you may use it here.

11.q: take it and carry it back to its place
11.note: Alternate translation: [take the chest and carry it back to its place]

12.note: Alternate translation: [men who built with stone and men who built with wood]

12.q: those who worked in iron and bronze
12.note: Alternate translation: [men who made things from iron and bronze]

13.note: Here the word “forward” represents progress, and the word “hands” represents their control. Alternate translation: [made progress under their supervision]

14.note: This is money that was collected in the chest but not needed for repairs.
This refers to the “utensils” and “spoons” listed later in the verse.

14.q: for all the days of Jehoiada
14.note: This idiom refers to the lifespan of Jehoiada. Alternate translation: [for as long as Jehoiada lived] or [throughout the lifetime of Jehoiada]

15.q: grew old and was full of days
15.note: These two phrases mean the same thing and emphasize how long he lived. Alternate translation: [became very old]
This idiom means he lived a long time.

16.note: Alternate translation: [among the tombs of the kings] or [among the graves of the kings]

16.q: because he had done good in Israel, toward God, and to God’s house
16.note: The nominal adjective “good” can be translated as an adjective. Alternate translation: [because he had done good things in Judah for God and for God’s temple]

17.note: Alternate translation: [gave honor to King Joash] or [honored the king]

17.q: Then the king listened to them
17.note: The following verse indicates that they wanted the king to serve idols instead of Yahweh, and he agreed. Alternate translation: [Then they persuaded the king to do what they wanted]

18.q: God’s anger came on Judah and Jerusalem
18.note: God’s anger is spoken of as something that covered over Judah and Jerusalem. Here the words “Judah” and “Jerusalem” are metonyms for the people who lived there. Alternate translation: [God became very angry with the people of Judah and Jerusalem] (See also: [Metonymy](ta:figs-metonymy))

19.note: Here the word “yet” indicates a contrast between God’s anger and his sending of the prophets to give them a chance to repent and avoid judgment.
The reflexive pronoun emphasizes that Yahweh was the one to whom they should turn.
Alternate translation: [the people refused to obey]

20.q: The Spirit of God came on Zechariah
20.note: This is an idiom which means that the Spirit of God influenced Zechariah and enabled him to prophesy. See how you translated a similar phrase in [2 Chronicles 15:1](ta:15).
This was not the same man as Zechariah son of Berechiah who wrote the Book of Zechariah.

20.q: Why do you transgress the commandments of Yahweh, so that you cannot prosper?
20.note: Zechariah asked this rhetorical question to rebuke the people. If it would be helpful in your language, you could express this question as a statement. Alternate translation: [You are transgressing the commandments of Yahweh, so that is why you cannot prosper.]

22.q: ignored the kindness that Jehoiada, Zechariah’s father, had done to him
22.note: Joash did not pay attention to the way that Jehoiada, Zechariah’s father, had been kind to Joash.
Alternate translation: [make you pay for the wrong you have done]

23.note: This phrase is used here to mark the beginning of a new part of the story. If your language has a way for doing this, you could consider using it here.

23.q: sent all the plunder from them
23.note: Alternate translation: [sent all the plunder from Judah and Jerusalem]

24.q: victory over a very great army
24.note: Alternate translation: [victory over the much larger army of Judah]

24.q: In this way the Arameans brought judgment on Joash
24.note: This refers to God’s judgment. This can be stated as an action. Alternate translation: [In this way God used the Arameans to judge Joash] (See also: [Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information](ta:figs-explicit))

25.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [they had severely wounded Joash]

25.q: because of the murder of the sons of Jehoiada
25.note: Alternate translation: [because he had murdered the sons of Jehoiada]

25.q: They killed him in his bed
25.note: Alternate translation: [The servants killed Joash in his bed]

26.note: These are the names of men.

26.q: Shimeath, an Ammonite woman … Shimrith, a Moabite woman
26.note: “Shimeath, from the country of Ammon … Shimrith, from the country of Moab.” These are the names of two women.

27.note: Alternate translation: [the record of what his sons did]

27.q: the important prophecies that were spoken about him
27.note: Alternate translation: [the important things the prophets spoke about him]
Here “see” alerts the reader to pay special attention to the information that follows.

27.q: the commentary on the book of the kings
27.note: This is a book which no longer exists.
